task: Given an ICP, list the most relevant discovery channels.
rationale: For Series B funding signals, Crunchbase and PitchBook are authoritative. LinkedIn provides headcount and title data. Exa provides semantic web search for press releases. Apollo provides contact info. Web search catches funding announcements not yet in Crunchbase.

task: Given an ICP, list the most relevant discovery channels.
rationale: For midwest manufacturing, Google Maps is the primary discovery channel (most manufacturers have GMB listings). LinkedIn provides headcount and leadership. Apollo provides contact info. Web search catches plant expansion announcements. ThomasNet is industry-specific.

task: Given an ICP, list the most relevant discovery channels.
rationale: For Singapore FinTech, LinkedIn is primary for headcount and titles. Crunchbase provides funding data. MAS Financial Institutions Directory provides license status. Exa for press releases and partnership announcements. Apollo for contact info.

task: Identify duplicate accounts across channels.
rationale: Matched on normalized domain (stripe.com). Name variations normalized. Source channels merged.

task: Given an ICP, list the most relevant discovery channels.
rationale: For Israeli-US cybersecurity, Crunchbase captures funding rounds. LinkedIn is essential for headcount and leadership titles. Exa finds press releases and partnership announcements. Apollo provides contact data. YC Directory catches early-stage Israeli startups (many are YC alums). Web search catches news not yet in databases.

task: Given an ICP, list the most relevant discovery channels.
rationale: For US healthtech with EHR integrations, LinkedIn finds leadership and hiring signals. Apollo provides contact data. Google Maps catches local clinics and hospitals. Exa finds product launch announcements. HL7/FHIR directories identify companies with integration capabilities. Web search for regulatory and compliance news.

task: Given an ICP, list the most relevant discovery channels.
rationale: For DACH logistics, LinkedIn is primary for headcount and titles (German executives are active). Apollo provides contact data. Google Maps finds warehouses and distribution centers. Exa catches partnership and expansion news. Local chambers of commerce directories are valuable for regional companies without strong web presence.

task: Given an ICP, list the most relevant discovery channels.
rationale: For Indian edtech, LinkedIn finds leadership. Crunchbase provides funding data. Apollo provides contact info. Exa catches product launches. Web search for regulatory changes (NEP 2020 impact). Tracxn is India-specific and often has better coverage of early-stage startups than Crunchbase.

task: Given an ICP, list the most relevant discovery channels.
rationale: For US proptech, LinkedIn finds leadership and hiring signals. Apollo provides contact data. Crunchbase tracks funding. Exa finds partnership announcements. Web search for market trend news. Zillow tech directory identifies companies in the real estate tech ecosystem.

task: Discover prospects using LinkedIn-specific search.

search_strategy.query: company_size:11-200 industry:computer_software currently_hiring:true title:VP Engineering OR CTO

rationale: LinkedIn Sales Navigator is the best channel for person-first discovery in dev tools. Filtering by 'currently hiring' catches companies with engineering expansion budgets. Sales Nav allows title + company size + industry compound filters.

task: Discover prospects using Apollo-specific search.

search_strategy.query: industry:saas revenue:5m-100m location:us,ca title:cro OR vp_sales intent:high

rationale: Apollo excels at contact-first discovery with verified emails and intent data. Their 'intent signals' feature identifies companies showing buying behavior. Apollo's B2B SaaS coverage is strongest in North America.

task: Cross-reference prospects found across multiple channels.
rationale: All four sources agree on domain. Funding and headcount from different sources provide triangulation. Technographics from BuiltWith add a dimension unavailable in other sources. Confidence weighted by source reliability.

task: Discover prospects with limited data availability.

search_strategy.query: nông nghiệp công nghệ Việt Nam
limitations: LinkedIn penetration in VN agriculture is <15%
Crunchbase coverage of VN startups is minimal
Most companies lack English-language web presence
workarounds: Scrape Google Maps for business listings
Cross-reference with Vietnam Chamber of Commerce

rationale: Vietnamese agriculture companies have minimal digital footprint in Western databases. Google Maps is the most reliable source. Vietnamese-language queries are essential. Expect lower yield and higher enrichment effort downstream.

task: Discover person prospects for a specific role.

search_strategy.supplemental: exa_search for 'CISO hired' OR 'CISO appointed' financial services 2026

rationale: CISO discovery is person-first, not company-first. LinkedIn Sales Navigator has the richest title data. Apollo adds verified contact info. Exa catches recent hires and appointments. Web search supplements with press releases about new CISO hires.

task: Discover prospects for a niche industry with strict compliance.
rationale: UK law firms are SRA-regulated and PECR applies to electronic marketing. Legal 500 and Chambers directories provide ranked firm lists. LinkedIn adds headcount and titles. All outreach must include opt-out mechanism. Legitimate interest basis is available for B2B under UK GDPR.

task: Discover company prospects via URL analysis.

discovery_result.note: Product subdomain — parent company is HashiCorp
Open-source project site — parent company is HashiCorp

rationale: URL analysis resolved three separate URLs to one company (HashiCorp). terraform.io and vaultproject.io are product sites. Parent company domain is hashicorp.com. Cross-referencing with LinkedIn/Crunchbase confirms single entity.

task: Discover prospects with technographic filters.
rationale: Technographic-first discovery requires BuiltWith or HG Insights as primary channels. BuiltWith detects client-side tech; HG Insights detects infrastructure spend. LinkedIn and Apollo add contact data but cannot filter by tech stack.

task: Discover prospects in a specific region with language constraints.

search_strategy.query: 製造業 東京 大阪
language_considerations: LinkedIn penetration in JP manufacturing is ~25%
Business culture requires formal outreach in Japanese

rationale: Japanese manufacturing companies have low LinkedIn penetration. Google Maps with Japanese-language queries is the most productive channel. Exa can search Japanese-language content. All outreach must be in Japanese with proper keigo (formal language).

task: Identify duplicate accounts with subtle variations.

dedup_result.name: SAP SE
dedup_result.notes: SAP Labs is a subsidiary — kept as separate entity for pipeline purposes if targeting subsidiary-level contacts

rationale: Domain normalization (sap.com, www.sap.com → sap.com) resolves 4 of 5 entries. 'SAP America Inc' is a regional subsidiary of SAP SE but shares the same domain. 'SAP Labs' is also a subsidiary — if targeting subsidiary-level contacts, keep separate; otherwise merge into parent.

task: Discover prospects using event-based signals.

search_strategy.supplemental: apollo for contacts at companies exhibiting at these events

rationale: Conference attendance is a high-intent signal. LinkedIn captures post-event engagement (posts, comments about the conference). Exa catches press coverage. Conference attendee/exhibitor lists (where available) are gold. Hiring CISO/VP Security after a conference often indicates new budget allocation.

task: Discover prospects for an account-based marketing campaign.

per_account_steps: 1. Lookup company on LinkedIn for headcount and titles
2. Enrich with Apollo for verified contacts

rationale: ABM requires deep research on a small number of accounts. Each account gets a dedicated discovery pass across all channels. Focus on multi-threading (multiple contacts per account) rather than volume.
